readings.c1s1:
''able.''

'''undiscernibleness''' (un-di-zėr′ni-bl-nes), ''n.'' Indiscernibleness.

'''undiscernibly''' (un-di-zėr′ni-bli), ''adv.'' Indiscernibly. ''Jer. Taylor'', Repentance, v. § 5.

'''undiscerning''' (un-di-zėr′ning), ''a.'' Not discerning; not making just distinctions; lacking judgment or the power of discrimination. ''Donne.''

'''undischarged''' (un-dis-chärjd′), ''a.'' Not discharged. {{smaller|(''a'') Not dismissed; not freed from obligation.}}
{{smaller block|Hold still in readiness and ''undischarged.''
{{right|''B. Jonson'', Sejanus, v. 3.}}}}
{{smaller|(''b'') Not fulfilled; not carried out; unexecuted: as, an ''undischarged'' duty.}}

'''undisciplinable''' (un-dis′i-plin-a-bl), ''a.'' Incapable of being disciplined. ''Sir M. Hale'', Of Self-Denial.

'''undisciplined''' (un-dis′i-plind), ''a.'' Not disciplined; not duly exercised and taught; not properly trained or brought to regularity and order; raw: as, ''undisciplined'' troops; ''undisciplined'' valor; ''undisciplined'' minds.
{{smaller block|An armed disciplined body is, in its essence, dangerous to liberty; ''undisciplined'', it is ruinous to society.
{{right|''Burke'', Speech on Army Estimates, 1790.}}}}

'''undisclose†''' (un-dis-klōz′), ''v. t.'' To refrain from disclosing; keep close or secret. ''Daniel.''

'''undiscomfited''' (un-dis-kum′fi-ted), ''a.'' Not discomfited.
{{smaller block|He may his cheere holde ''undescounfited.''
{{right|''Chaucer'', Boëthius, i. meter 4.}}}}

'''undiscording''' (un-dis-kôr′ding), ''a.'' Not discording; not disagreeing; not discordant in sound; harmonious. [Rare.]
readings.c1s2:
{{smaller block|With ''undiscording'' voice.
{{right|''Milton'', Solemn Music, l. 17.}}}}

'''undiscoursed''' (un-dis-kōrst′), ''a.'' Not discoursed about; not made the subject of talk or discussion; silent. [Rare.]
{{smaller block|We would submit to all with indefinite and ''undiscoursed'' obedience.
{{right|''Bp. Hacket'', Abp. Williams, i. 130. ''(Davies.)''}}}}

'''undiscoverable''' (un-dis-kuv′ėr-a̤-bl), ''a.'' That cannot be discovered or found out: as, ''undiscoverable'' principles.

'''undiscoverably''' (un-dis-kuv′ėr-a̤-bli), ''adv.'' In a manner not to be discovered. ''Milton'', Tetrachordon.

'''undiscovered''' (un-dis-kuv′ėrd), ''a.'' Not discovered; not seen; not descried; not laid open to view; lying hid.
{{smaller block|<poem>The ''undiscover’d'' country, from whose bourn
No traveller returns.</poem>
{{right|''Shak.'', Hamlet, iii. 1. 79.}}}}

'''undiscreet†''' (un-dis-krēt′), ''a.'' [Early mod. E. also ''undiscrete''; < ME. ''undiscreet''; < ''un-''<sup>1</sup> + ''discreet''.] Indiscreet.
{{smaller block|So ''undiscreet'' of governaunce.
{{right|''Chaucer'', Nun’s Priest’s Tale, l. 614.}}
The ''undiscrete'' hastinesse of the emperour Claudius caused hym to be noted for foolisshe.
{{right|''Sir T. Elyot'', The Governour, ii. 6.}}}}

'''undiscreetly†''' (un-dis-krēt′li), ''adv.'' Indiscreetly. ''Tyndale'', Ans. to Sir T. More, etc. (Parker Soc., 1850), p. 95.

'''undiscreetness''' (un-dis-krēt′nes), ''n.'' Indiscretion; imprudence. ''Udall'', tr. of Apophthegms of Erasmus, p. 328.

'''undiscretion†''' (un-dis-kresh′o̤n), ''n.'' [< ME. ''undiscretion''; < ''un-''<sup>1</sup> + ''discretion''.] Indiscretion. ''Lydgate'', Story of Thebes, iii.

'''undiscriminating''' (un-dis-krim′i-nā-ting), ''a.'' Not discriminating; not distinguishing or making a difference. ''Cowper'', Odyssey, xxii.

'''undiscussed''' (un-dis-kust′), ''a.'' Not discussed; not argued or debated. ''Bp. Hall'', Christ Transfigured, ii.

'''undisguisable''' (un-dis-gī′za̤-bl), ''a.'' Incapable of being disguised. ''Quarterly Rev.''

'''undisguised''' (un-dis-gīzd′), ''a.'' Not disguised; not covered with a mask or with a false appearance; hence, open; frank; candid; plain; artless: as, ''undisguised'' anxiety.
{{smaller block|Plaine English ''undisguised.'' ''The Isle of Ladies'', l. 1450.

Himself he view’d with ''undisguised'' respect.
{{right|''Crabbe'', Tales, Works, IV. 129.}}}}

'''undisguisedly''' (un-dis-gī′zed-li), ''adv.'' In an undisguised manner; openly; frankly.

'''undishonored''' (un-dis-on′o̤rd), ''a.'' Not dishonored; not disgraced. ''Shak.'', C. of E., ii. 2. 148.

'''undisjoined''' (un-dis-joind′), ''a.'' Not disjoined; not separated or parted. ''Cowper.''

'''undisputableness''' (un-dis-pū′- or un-dis′pū-ta-bl-nes), ''n.'' The quality or state of being undisputable.

'''undisputably''' (un-dis-pū′- or un-dis′pū-ta-bli), ''adv.'' Indisputably. ''The Engineer'', LXX. 31. [Rare.]

'''undisputed''' (un-dis-pū′ted), ''a.'' Not disputed; not contested; not called in question: as, an ''undisputed'' title; ''undisputed'' truth. ''Congreve'', Hymn to Harmony.

'''undisputedly''' (un-dis-pū′ted-li), ''adv.'' In an undisputed manner; indisputably.

'''undissembled''' (un-di-sem′bld), ''a.'' Not dissembled; open; undisguised; unfeigned.
{{smaller block|''Undissembled'' and unlimited veneration for the Holy Scriptures.
{{right|''Bp. Atterbury'', Sermons, I. xviii.}}}}

'''undissipated''' (un-dis′i-pā-ted), ''a.'' Not dissipated; not scattered. ''Boyle.''

'''undissolvable''' (un-di-zol′va-bl), ''a.'' '''1.''' Incapable of being dissolved or melted.—'''2.''' Incapable of being loosened or broken: as, the ''undissolvable'' ties of friendship. ''Rowe'', Tamerlane, iii.

'''undissolved''' (un-di-zolvd′), ''a.'' Not dissolved; not melted; not loosened, dispelled, broken, etc. ''Tennyson'', Day-Dream.

'''undissolving''' (un-di-zol′ving), ''a.'' Not dissolving; not melting; not loosening.
{{smaller block|To link soft hearts in ''undissolving'' bands.
{{right|''Beaumont'', Masque of Inner-Temple.}}}}

'''undistempered''' (un-dis-tem′pėrd), ''a.'' Free from distemper, disease, or perturbation; free from any disordering influence.
{{smaller block|Any unprejudiced and ''undistempered'' mind.
{{right|''Barrow'', III. 36.}}}}

'''undistinctive''' (un-dis-tingk′tiv), ''a.'' Undiscriminating; making no distinctions; impartial.
{{smaller block|''Undistinctive'' Death.
{{right|''Dickens.''}}}}

'''undistinctly†''' (un-dis-tingkt′li), ''adv.'' Indistinctly. ''Hooker'', Eccles. Polity, v. § 68.

'''undistinguishable''' (un-dis-ting′gwish-a-bl), ''a.'' Not distinguishable; indistinguishable.
{{smaller block|<poem>The quaint mazes in the wanton green
For lack of tread are ''undistinguishable''.</poem>}}

'''undistinguishableness''' (un-dis-ting′gwish-a̤-bl-nes), ''n.'' The state or character of being undistinguishable. ''Nature'', XLIII. 159.

'''undistinguishably''' (un-dis-ting′gwish-a̤-bli), ''adv.'' Indistinguishably.

'''undistinguished''' (un-dis-ting′gwisht), ''a.'' '''1.''' Not distinguished; not so marked as to be distinctly known from another; not discerned or discriminated.

'''ndividedness''' (un-di-vī′ded-nes), ''n.'' The quality or state of being undivided; wholeness.

'''ndividual†''' (un-di-vid′ū-al), ''a.'' [< ''un-''<sup>1</sup> + ''dividual.'' Cf. ''individual.''] Not capable of being divided; indivisible.

{{smaller block|<poem>The quaint mazes in the wanton green
For lack of tread are ''undistinguishable''.</poem> {{right|''Shak.'', M. N. D., ii. 1. 100.}}}}

'''undistinguishableness''' (un-dis-ting′gwish-a̤-bl-nes), ''n.'' The state or character of being undistinguishable. ''Nature'', XLIII. 159.

'''undistinguishably''' (un-dis-ting′gwish-a̤-bli), ''adv.'' Indistinguishably.

'''undistinguished''' (un-dis-ting′gwisht), ''a.'' '''1.''' Not distinguished; not so marked as to be distinctly known from another; not discerned or discriminated. {{smaller block|{{right|''Addison'', Thoughts in Westminster Abbey.}}
His ashes ''undistinguished'' lie.
{{right|''Scott'', L. of L. M., v. 2.}}
<poem>The slopes and rills in ''undistinguished'' gray
Melt away.</poem>
{{right|''Browning'', Love Among the Ruins.}}}}
'''2.''' Not treated with distinction or marked respect. ''Pope.''—'''3.''' Not separated from others by extraordinary qualities; not famous; not distinguished by particular eminence: as, ''undistinguished'' people.—'''4.''' Not having an air of distinction: as, an ''undistinguished'' appearance or mien.

'''undistinguishing''' (un-dis-ting′gwish-ing), ''a.'' Making no difference; not discriminating: as, ''undistinguishing'' favor.
{{smaller block|A general ''undistinguishing'' suspicion is altogether as apt to mislead a man as a too easy and unwary credulity.
{{right|''Bp. Atterbury'', Sermons, I. v.}}}}

'''undistracted''' (un-dis-trak′ted), ''a.'' Not distracted; not perplexed by contrariety or variety of thoughts, desires, or concerns. ''Boyle'', Works, I. 276.

'''undistractedly''' (un-dis-trak′ted-li), ''adv.'' Without distraction. ''Boyle'', Works, I. 254.

'''undistractedness''' (un-dis-trak′ted-nes), ''n.'' The state of being undistracted. ''Boyle'', Works, I. 3.

'''undistracting''' (un-dis-trak′ting), ''a.'' Not distracting; not confusing the mind by drawing it toward a variety of objects. ''Leighton'', Expos. on Psalm xix.

'''undisturbed''' (un-dis-tėrbd′), ''a.'' '''1.''' Free from disturbance or interruption; not molested or hindered: as, ''undisturbed'' with company or noise; ''undisturbed'' friendly relations.—'''2.''' Not agitated; hence, free from perturbation of mind; calm; tranquil; placid; serene; composed: as, ''undisturbed'' by danger.
{{smaller block|The ''undisturbed'' and silent waters.{{right|''Dryden.''}}}}
='''Syn.''' {{smaller|Quiet, peaceful, unmoved, unruffled.}}

'''undisturbedly''' (un-dis-tėr′bed-li), ''adv.'' In an undisturbed or tranquil manner; calmly; peacefully. ''Locke.''

'''undisturbedness''' (un-dis-tėr′bed-nes), ''n.'' The state of being undisturbed; calmness; peacefulness.

'''undiversified''' (un-di-vėr′si-fīd), ''a.'' Not diversified; not varied; uniform.
{{smaller block|A particle of mere ''undiversified'' matter.{{right|''Dr. T. Cogan'', On the Passions, note R.}}}}

'''undiverted''' (un-di-vėr′ted), ''a.'' '''1.''' Not diverted; not turned aside.
{{smaller block|These grounds have not any patent passages, . . . and therefore must suffer the greatest part of it (the river) to run by them ''undiverted.''{{right|''Boyle'', Works, II. 408.}}

Her young friend, apparently, was an interesting study; she wished to pursue it ''undiverted.'' {{right|''H. James, Jr.'', Pass. Pilgrim, p. 221.}}}}
'''2.''' Not amused; not entertained or pleased.

{{smaller block|The reader, however, may not be ''undiverted'' with its unaffected simplicity and pathos. {{right|''Wakefield'', Memoirs, p. 8.}}}}

'''undivestedly''' (un-di-ves′ted-li), ''adv.'' With the absence (of); free. [Erroneous.]

{{smaller block|You will (as ''undivestedly'' as possible of favour or resentment) tell me what you would have me do. {{right|''Richardson'', Clarissa Harlowe, ii. 64. (''Davies.'')}}}}

'''undividable''' (un-di-vī′dạ-bl), ''a.'' and ''n.'' '''I.''' ''a.'' Incapable of being divided or separated; indivisible. ''Shak.'', C. of E., ii. 2. 124.

'''II.''' ''n.'' Something which cannot be divided.

{{smaller block|Reducing the ''undivideables'' into money. {{right|''Jarvis'', tr. of Don Quixote, II. v. 9.}}}}

'''undivided''' (un-di-vī′ded), ''a.'' '''1.''' Not divided; not separated or disunited; unbroken; whole: as, ''undivided'' attention.

{{smaller block|God should be the object of our ''undivided'' respect. {{right|''J. Edwards'', Works, IV. 177.}}}}
'''2.''' Not made separate and limited to a particular sum: as, to own an ''undivided'' share of a business.—'''3.''' In ''bot.'', not lobed, cleft, or branched.—'''4.''' In ''entom.'', composed of a single piece: as, an ''undivided'' pygidium.

'''undividedly''' (un-di-vī′ded-li), ''adv.'' Without division or separation; unbrokenly.

{{smaller block|Creation, nature, religion, law, and policy make them [man and wife] ''undividedly'' one. {{right|''Feltham'', On St. Luke xiv. 20.}}}}

'''ndividedness''' (un-di-vī′ded-nes), ''n.'' The quality or state of being undivided; wholeness.

'''ndividual†''' (un-di-vid′ū-al), ''a.'' [< ''un-''<sup>1</sup> + ''dividual.'' Cf. ''individual.''] Not capable of being divided; indivisible.<noinclude><references/></noinclude>
